title: BlockPIM: Optimizing Memory Management for PIM-enabled Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: PIM architectures alleviate memory bandwidth bottlenecks in LLM decode phase but fragmented data layout limits end-to-end acceleration, especially for long-context sequences where memory utilization remains suboptimal.
motivation: Long-context LLM inference is increasingly important for reasoning and document understanding; PIM can unlock this workload if memory layout and access patterns are optimized.
method: Proposes cross-channel block memory layout strategy maximizing utilization and eliminating context length constraints; introduces cross-channel attention computation compatible with current PIM architecture to support distributed operations.
key_novelty: Cross-channel block memory layout strategy for fragmented data consolidation in PIM, enabling efficient long-context LLM inference.
contributions: Cross-channel block memory layout strategy for maximum utilization
Elimination of context length constraints in PIM-based LLM inference
Cross-channel attention computation scheme compatible with current PIM
62% average throughput increase vs. existing PIM solutions

metrics.speedup: 62% throughput increase vs. state-of-the-art PIM solutions

baselines: Existing state-of-the-art PIM solutions for LLM inference
limitations: Limited to PIM-enabled architectures; applicability to other memory hierarchies not discussed.
primary_theme: Cross-channel block memory layout for PIM-based long-context LLM inference
